item.title: The Vegetarian
item.description: This was Mat Steeples’s choice for October’s Trafalgar Street Book Club (TSBC). Han Kang won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Literature, and the book itself won the International Booker Prize and a number of other literary awards. Suffice it to say, it had a lot to live up to. I suppose it’s great for sales when a book gets this kind of attention, but it also inevitably means that one approaches it with sky-high expectations. Han Kang is one of Korea’s leading novelists, but I had not heard of her before Mat chose her book. It’s not surprising since I’m barely aware of the current literary scene and pay no attention to fiction book awards. It is fair to say that I would have been unlikely to read it if it hadn’t been for the TSBC, but I guess that’s the joy of a book club: to be taken out of one’s rut and exposed to new things. I ordered my copy from Amazon. It’s a thin paperback of 183 pages, well under the TSBC maximum of 300, with a very dull monochrome cover. I guess you don’t need to be gaudy when you’ve won the Nobel Prize. I read it over four days.
